expectations.text: Identifies free-mail domains as the cause of the 4,100-person account, and instructs excluding free-mail-class domains from account matching.
expectations.evidence: "The 4,100-person account is a free-mail domain caught by naive domain matching." and "exclude every one of those domains from account resolution"

expectations.text: Explains that free-mail domains identify no company, so matching on them collapses strangers into one account.
expectations.evidence: "Free-mail domains identify no company and must never enter account matching." / "Domain-based rollup with no exclusion list collapses every stranger sharing a public webmail domain into one 'account.'"

expectations.text: Diagnoses the one-person accounts as signup domains that never resolved to a company, and recommends enrichment or manual matching as the fallback.
expectations.evidence: "add an enrichment step (Clearbit-class or manual) to catch the subsidiary/regional-TLD cases"

expectations.text: Requires reporting what share of the population actually resolved to an account.
expectations.evidence: "publish the resolved share (e.g., \"68% of paid-tier accounts resolved to a verified company; 32% are single-domain matches, unverified\")"

expectations.text: Forbids presenting an account-level rate computed from a partially resolved population without stating that share.
expectations.evidence: "Never publish Y% alone — an account-level rate computed over a partially resolved population, presented without the resolution share, is exactly the number that gets someone burned in the next board deck."

expectations.text: States that in a company-buying motion every event must carry account_id alongside user_id.
expectations.evidence: No explicit general rule stating every event must carry account_id alongside user_id appears; the transcript only describes account_id resolution and touch-event non-null filtering.

expectations.text: Identifies this as the both-at-once motion, instrumenting person-level everywhere and rolling up to account only where an org object genuinely exists.
expectations.evidence: "Arbordyne's motion is 'both at once' ... person-level and account-level tracking both have to exist and get joined only where a real company resolves"

expectations.text: States that the influenced-pipeline report depends on the CRM being able to carry an account-level touch record, and that a lead source field alone cannot honestly support it.
expectations.evidence: "Why the lead-source field can't answer sales' question ... Push these into the CRM as a related-list/activity object on the Account, not a single field"

expectations.text: Settles that dependency before the report is promised to sales, rather than after.
expectations.evidence: "Don't ship the report before step 3 lands. A version built on the current lead-source field will look plausible and be wrong in a way nobody downstream can detect"
